sugestoes.texto: WHAT: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offset to 0 for forward cursors but passes it through for is_prev cursors (start_offset = max(0,offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset). WHY: Inconsistent handling returns first page for crafted forward negative cursor instead of error and still passes negative start to queryset[offset:stop] for prev cursors where Django forbids negative indexing (AssertionError/500) plus line 192 length check uses raw offset causing wrong trim.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(value)) and value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value, copying integer-id Paginator semantics instead of DateTimePaginator datetime conversion. WHY: Caller passes order_by='-datetime' (organization_auditlogs.py:80) so getattr returns datetime which crashes math.floor with TypeError and datetime-column filtering with int cursor_value produces wrong results/DB error — broken paginator contract.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features allows attacker-controlled cursor.offset<0 to reach queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start, falsely claimed safe because Django handles it and permissions are at queryset level. WHY: Cursor offset is parsed from user-supplied ?cursor= string with no negative validation (Cursor.__init__ just int(offset)); crafted negative offset triggers unhandled AssertionError (DoS/500) or out-of-bounds pagination window bypass, reachable via ?optimized_pagination=true gated only on has_global_access.

WHAT: Changed line 71 dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check though member is Optional. WHY: A request reaching get() with member=None and request.user.is_superuser falsy raises AttributeError and returns 500 instead of a paginated response. HOW: Guard with (organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access).

issues.descricao: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes negative cursor offsets straight into Django queryset slicing, which Django does not support, so requests with a negative offset raise an error instead of returning a page.
issues.textoGolden: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

comentarios.texto: The advanced negative-offset branch passes a negative slice start directly to a Django QuerySet, which does not support negative indexing. A cursor such as 0:-1:0 is accepted by Cursor.from_string but crashes the optimized audit-log request instead of providing reverse pagination. Reject negative offsets with BadPaginationError or implement reverse traversal using nonnegative slices and reversed ordering.

The comment claiming that Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative indices. This branch passes cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop], so it raises rather than supplying the documented negative-offset pagination. Correct the negative-offset support claims here, in the class docstring, and in the new BasePaginator boundary-handling comment (or implement actual supported boundary handling) so callers are not promised a pagination mode that the underlying queryset cannot provide.

Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds. Passing a negative cursor offset directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises an exception instead of enabling advanced pagination. Validate or normalize negative offsets before slicing, or implement reverse traversal through ordering/filtering rather than negative slices.

issues.descricao: The comment added to BasePaginator claims negative offsets are allowed and safely handled by the queryset, but the code clamps non-prev offsets to zero and leaves prev offsets as before, so the comment misdescribes the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: The added comment says this change will "allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination ... safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions", but the statement it annotates, line 182, is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` — it clamps negative offsets to 0, i.e. it does the opposite of what the comment claims and leaves the 'negative offset' (offset < 0) paging behaviour exactly as before. The comment is now untrue for the code it sits on; either drop the 'allow negative offsets' wording or make the code actually permit them.

The comment declares this change `allow[s] negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination`, but the actual computation is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which clamps non-prev offsets at 0 — i.e. it never permits a negative offset. The declared optimization is a no-op relative to the original `queryset[offset:stop]`; the comment describes behavior the code does not have.

BasePaginator now passes the raw `offset` to the slice whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). A negative offset from a user-supplied prev cursor therefore reaches `queryset[negative:stop]`, which Django rejects. This crashes every endpoint that uses BasePaginator. Fix: always use `max(0, offset)`, or validate the offset when the cursor is parsed.

issues.descricao: The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring claims streamlined boundary handling, an optimized query path and backward compatibility that the implementation, a copy of BasePaginator plus a negative-offset branch, does not provide.

comentarios.texto: Docstring lists 'Streamlined boundary condition handling', 'Optimized query path for large datasets', and 'maintaining backward compatibility', but get_result (845-886) is a copy of BasePaginator with only a negative-offset branch added — no streamlined handling or optimized path exists, and negative-offset slicing breaks prior cursor semantics. Doc describes behavior the function does not produce — align doc to code or implement the claimed handling.

issues.descricao: OptimizedCursorPaginator computes cursor keys with math.floor/ceil on the raw attribute, but the audit log endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime', so building the cursor raises TypeError for any non-empty result.
issues.textoGolden: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

comentarios.texto: OptimizedCursorPaginator requires numeric integer keys (get_item_key uses math.floor/ceil + int, cursor_value defaults to 0) but is instantiated here with order_by="-datetime". This mismatched producer/consumer contract breaks pagination for datetime-ordered audit logs. Fix: do not use OptimizedCursorPaginator for datetime ordering; keep DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator datetime-aware.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor mishandles datetime ordering by calling math.floor/ceil directly on a datetime and returning raw int cursor value. WHY: Used with order_by="-datetime" it crashes with TypeError on floor(datetime) when building cursors and filters the datetime column against an int in build_queryset, breaking pagination. HOW: Copy DateTimePaginator logic — timestamp via strftime/multiplier with floor/ceil and convert cursor value back with datetime.fromtimestamp.

The optimized branch selects a numeric-key paginator while ordering by the datetime field. On any nonempty first page, build_cursor invokes OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key, which calls math.ceil on a datetime and raises TypeError; nonzero cursors also lack the datetime conversion provided by DateTimePaginator. Make the optimized paginator inherit DateTimePaginator or preserve its timestamp encoding and decoding.

issues.descricao: The audit log endpoint always dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access, which crashes with AttributeError for authorized token requests that have no member, even on the default pagination path.
issues.textoGolden: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

comentarios.texto: The unconditional advanced-access check dereferences organization_context.member although RpcUserOrganizationContext permits member=None. Authorized non-member organization-token requests therefore raise AttributeError even when optimized_pagination is absent, instead of returning audit logs through the existing paginator. Guard the optional member and evaluate eligibility only when optimized pagination is requested.

issues.descricao: The comments and enable_advanced variable describe the optimized_pagination path as a performance optimization for administrators, hiding that it enables negative-offset slicing.

comentarios.texto: The comments describe a 'performance optimization' for 'authorized administrators', and the variable is named enable_advanced. In fact it opts into negative-offset slicing, and the optimized_pagination query parameter gates it. The names and comments hide what the flag actually enables. Rename them to say what is enabled, or remove the path.

issues.descricao: A user-controlled optimized_pagination flag lets any member with global access switch to a paginator that accepts unvalidated negative cursor offsets, widening the attack surface and causing server errors.

comentarios.texto: A user-controlled `optimized_pagination` query flag switches the endpoint to a paginator that accepts attacker-supplied negative cursor offsets. This is available to any user with global access, not only to real admins. It widens the attack surface for unvalidated cursor offsets and causes server errors. The comment 'permissions are checked at the queryset level' is not backed by any check in the paginator. Fix: remove the optimized path, or have the paginator validate and clamp offsets.

issues.descricao: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offsets only for next cursors; a prev cursor with a negative offset is passed straight into the queryset slice, which Django rejects with an error (500) on every paginated endpoint.
The new comment in Cursor says negative offsets are allowed to enable efficient reverse pagination, but the constructor only calls int(offset) and provides no such behaviour.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value, which is then compared against the datetime column, so next/prev cursor pagination of audit logs breaks.
Comments in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result claim Django handles negative slicing and that permissions are checked at the queryset level; both are false.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which is off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 yields 3 instead of 2) and yields 1 for 0 handled separately but 2 for exactly one page. WHY: next clamps to user_count so UI navigates to an empty trailing page (offset == total) with currentPage == totalPages showing empty members. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), e.g. Math.ceil(this.get(user_count)/this.get(limit)).

WHAT: add_members splits usernames on comma without stripping whitespace, so 'user1, user2' looks up ' user2' via User.find_by_username and silently skips it. WHY: user-selector input joins with commas/spaces so the second and later usernames fail to be added with no error. HOW: strip each token (username.strip or username.strip!) before lookup and skip blanks.

WHAT: members action takes user-controlled limit/offset with no cap or validation (limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i). WHY: attacker can request limit=1000000 to force order+limit huge member serialization in one request, causing memory/CPU blowup on large groups. HOW: clamp limit to a max (e.g. min(limit, 200)) and sanitize negative/zero values.

WHAT: remove_member automatic-group test issues xhr :put while routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE and add_members to PUT. WHY: controller-action spec bypasses routing so it never verifies the DELETE route wiring and gives false confidence the guard is reachable via the real verb. HOW: change to xhr :delete, :remove_member to match config/routes.rb.

WHAT: add_members/remove_member read params.require(:group_id) but the routes define member routes (/admin/groups/:id/members) so the id arrives as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. WHY: Real requests from group.js (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json`) raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and member add/remove is broken; specs pass only because they inject group_id directly bypassing routing. HOW: Read the id the route provides (e.g. Group.find(params[:id] || params[:group_id])) or declare the routes as collection/with explicit :group_id segment.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
Admin remove_member calls group.users.delete with a raw integer id, which raises RecordNotFound (404/500) when the user is not or no longer a member, e.g. on concurrent removal.
Admin remove_member deletes memberships with group.users.delete, which skips GroupUser callbacks, so the cached groups.user_count is never decremented and stays inflated.
Group member pagination is off by one when user_count is a multiple of limit: Next moves to offset == user_count and shows an empty page.
`add_members` runs one User query per username; load all users with a single `User.where(username: ...)` query.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} so no column is set despite the comment claiming to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany with no data is a validation error/no-op, aborting or wasting the post-cache-warm touch and leaving the cache-status timestamp stale. HOW: Pass an explicit touch field e.g. updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() }).

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars while disconnectMutation does (onSettled invalidate). WHY: After deleting cache the enriched cacheUpdatedAt stays cached in the tRPC query so the dropdown keeps showing the old Last updated timestamp until manual reload. HOW: Mirror disconnect logic — await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate() in deleteCache onSuccess/onSettled.

WHAT: sed -i '' -E uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: Fails on GNU/Linux (sed: can't read : No such file or directory) so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux dev machines. HOW: Branch on uname or use a portable update (e.g. sed -i.bak / awk / perl -pi -e).

WHAT: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved against the caller's CWD, not the script location. WHY: Running from repo root vs scripts/ writes/creates the wrong .env (or parent-dir .env), silently misconfiguring GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. HOW: Resolve relative to the script dir, e.g. SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd); ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env".

issues.descricao: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object, so Prisma does not refresh the @updatedAt timestamp and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never reflects the cache refresh.
issues.textoGolden: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany rejects empty data (validation error) or no-ops without touching @updatedAt, so the refresh path throws or silently leaves updatedAt stale. HOW: pass an explicit touch field e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() }.

Comment claims "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt" but call passes empty object {} as data, so nothing is updated (Prisma updateMany with empty data is a no-op/error). Fix comment or pass { updatedAt: new Date() } to match the stated intent.

updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {}. Prisma updateMany throws when data is empty, so this line throws on every resync after the cache write. Pass an explicit touch e.g. { updatedAt: new Date() } instead of {}.

issues.descricao: After deleting the calendar cache, CredentialActionsDropdown does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so where no parent refetch callback is passed the stale cache status and delete action remain visible.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query, while the sibling `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates it in `onSettled`. WHY: the 'Cache Status' row in the dropdown is rendered from the cached `connectedCalendars` result; after deleting the cache the query is not refetched, so the deleted status/last-updated entry stays visible and stale in the UI. HOW: invalidate the query in the cache-deletion mutation as well, e.g. `const utils = trpc.useUtils(); onSuccess: async () => { ...; await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(); }`.

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only calls onSuccess?.() and never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation onSettled. WHY: cacheUpdatedAt stays stale after deletion so UI keeps showing old Last updated and delete action until manual refetch. HOW: add onSettled invalidate of connectedCalendars like disconnect does.

Successful cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. The wrapper forwards only an optional parent onChanged callback and disables window-focus refetch, so the deleted cache continues to appear present with its old timestamp and delete action. Invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars on successful deletion.

issues.descricao: The cache 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale instead of the user's locale, so non-US users see US-style dates in an otherwise translated label.
issues.textoGolden: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

comentarios.texto: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded "en-US" locale (new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)), so every user — regardless of their locale — sees a US-style date/time while the surrounding label is translated. Use the app's locale-aware date formatting helper (the user's current locale) instead of pinning en-US.

Date format hard-coded to "en-US" via Intl.DateTimeFormat while surrounding strings use t()/useLocale. Users in other locales see US short date/time. Use the active locale from useLocale/i18n instead of hard-coding "en-US".

The cache timestamp is always formatted with "en-US", even though the surrounding label uses the user's selected translation locale. Users in other locales therefore see US month/day ordering and time conventions inside an otherwise localized message, potentially misreading the last-update date. Use the active application locale for Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of hard-coding en-US.

issues.descricao: The calendar cache migration keeps a generated warning saying updatedAt has no default and cannot be added to a non-empty table, although the SQL adds it with DEFAULT NOW().

comentarios.texto: This warning says updatedAt is added without a default and cannot be added to a nonempty table, but the migration actually supplies DEFAULT NOW(), explicitly handling existing rows. Remove or correct the warning so operators reviewing the migration are not incorrectly told that existing data makes it unsafe to run.

issues.descricao: The test-gcal-webhooks.sh cleanup function always exits 0, including when called from the failure paths, so the script reports success when the tunnel could not be set up.

comentarios.texto: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, and it is also called on the failure paths (rate limit hit, failed to extract the URL). The script therefore reports success even though the tunnel failed and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was never updated. Have `cleanup` take an exit code, and pass 1 from the failure paths.

cleanup() always ends in `exit 0`, and both failure paths (rate-limit at lines 46-50 and 'Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL' at lines 56-59) call cleanup. So a script named test-gcal-webhooks that did not actually obtain the tunnel URL / update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL still exits with status 0, letting any automation treat the run as successful even though the setup it verifies failed. On the failure branches the script should exit non-zero (e.g. `exit 1`) so failure is observable; only the SIGINT/SIGTERM interactive shutdown should exit 0.

issues.descricao: The webhook test script updates .env with the macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax, which fails on Linux GNU sed and leaves GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged.
issues.textoGolden: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `sed -i '' -E 's|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|' "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS `sed -i ''` form. WHY: under GNU sed (typical Linux dev/CI environment) the empty `''` is consumed as the script operand and the command errors, so the existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line is never replaced and the tunnel URL is not written to the env file. HOW: use a portable invocation, e.g. `sed -i.bak -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` (or branch on `uname`).

The environment update uses BSD sed's `-i ''` syntax, which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, the script leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it was updated, preventing webhooks from reaching the new tunnel. Use a portable replacement strategy or select the in-place syntax based on the available sed implementation and check its exit status.

When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists, `sed -i ''` uses BSD/macOS syntax and fails under GNU sed on Linux. The script nevertheless prints that the URL was updated and keeps the tunnel running, leaving webhooks configured with the old URL. Use a portable replacement approach (or select the appropriate sed syntax) and only announce success after the edit succeeds.

issues.descricao: deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error when the credential is missing or not owned by the user, so tRPC returns a 500 instead of a structured FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error.
issues.textoGolden: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.

issues.descricao: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.
The dev script writes tunnelmole output to a fixed /tmp/tmole.log, so a local attacker's symlink at that path could make it overwrite an arbitrary file.

The new test-gcal-webhooks.sh writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to '../.env' relative to the current directory, so running it from the repo root creates/edits a .env above the repo and the app never sees the URL.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: immediateDelete path POSTs cancel to SendGrid then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: Leaves an orphan scheduled=true row after workflow/step delete and reschedule callers (workflows.tsx:214,521 handleNewBooking.ts:968) so DB claims scheduled while SendGrid is cancelled. HOW: Delete the prisma row after successful cancel when immediateDelete is true.

WHAT: for-loop awaits SendGrid cancel per reminder and only after the loop awaits collected deletes; any throw jumps to catch and skips Promise.all. WHY: Single SendGrid failure aborts remaining cancels and discards already-queued deletes so cancelled emails are neither cancelled nor cleaned up. HOW: Per-reminder try/catch with finally-awaited deletes or Promise.allSettled.

WHAT: forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await and results are not added to prismaPromises. WHY: Handler returns before cancelled=true/delete persists and async errors are swallowed inside managers, so cancelled bookings can still send reminders. HOW: Collect promises and await Promise.all.

WHAT: try/catch wraps forEach of async deletes without await. WHY: forEach does not propagate async rejections so catch never fires and cancellations run fire-and-forget during reschedule, leaving old reminders active. HOW: Use for..of with await or Promise.all inside try.

WHAT: Awaited SendGrid cancel inside for..of over remindersToCancel issues N sequential network calls. WHY: Cron latency grows O(N) with cancelled-reminder count, delaying the 72h scheduling pass below. HOW: Fire cancels concurrently with Promise.all/pool.

WHAT: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now awaits twilio.cancelSMS before the prisma delete in the same try block, so a Twilio failure skips the DB delete. WHY: Previously the caller deleted the reminder row independently even when the Twilio cancel threw (manager swallowed), but now a transient Twilio error leaves a scheduled SMS row with no cancelled flag and no retry, so the SMS is still sent for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. HOW: Delete the row independently of Twilio result (or mark cancelled and retry), e.g. move the prisma delete outside the Twilio try or into a finally.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: Conditional include method is named include_website_name without trailing ? while AMS and all sibling predicates use include_<attr>? . WHY: The serializer framework never calls the misnamed predicate so website_name is always serialized (or never correctly gated), breaking the website.present? contract. HOW: Rename to def include_website_name? to match convention.

WHAT: Same-domain website_name is built as website_host + URI(website).path, dropping query string, fragment, and port (and not normalizing case). WHY: A same-domain URL like http://example.com/user?tab=about#bio displays as example.com/user, losing the distinguishing path and showing wrong/truncated output contrary to complete-path intent.

WHAT: The same-domain check only matches when the website host is the parent of the instance host, so a website that is a subdomain of the instance never shows its path. WHY: Line 149 tests discourse_host.ends_with?(website_host), which is false when website_host is longer (e.g. website forum.example.com with instance example.com), so it returns bare host and drops the distinguishing path. HOW: Also match the reverse direction, e.g. website_host.ends_with?("." + discourse_host), before falling back to bare host.

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. With an instance hostname of example.com and a valid website of http://EXAMPLE.COM/user, neither the exact-host nor suffix comparison matches, so the profile displays only EXAMPLE.COM instead of the requested path. Normalize both hostnames to lowercase for comparison while preserving the desired display spelling.

issues.descricao: website_name strips only the first label to decide same-domain, so unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes (co.uk, github.io) are treated as the instance domain and shown with full path.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `elsif` branch treats the last two dot-segments as the registrable domain, so multi-part public suffixes are mis-compared. WHY: for e.g. website_host='example.co.uk' and discourse_host='forum.co.uk' both have 3 segments, the branch compares `'co.uk' == 'co.uk'`, concludes the domains match, and returns `website_host + path`, even though example.co.uk and forum.co.uk are unrelated sites — the display then shows a path that does not belong to the instance domain, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: compare against a public-suffix-aware registrable domain (e.g. use the PublicSuffix list) or require at least the full suffix before treating hosts as the same domain, instead of blindly taking `split('.')[1..-1]`.

Comparing all labels except the first incorrectly treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, with instance host `forum.co.uk` and website `https://unrelated.co.uk/user`, this returns `unrelated.co.uk/user` rather than the unrelated-site host-only label. Both hosts have three labels and their suffixes are `co.uk`, so this branch mistakes the public suffix for a shared site domain. Use registrable-domain-aware comparison (or a narrower explicit host relationship) before including the path.

The same-label-count branch treats two hosts as the same domain when everything after the first label matches. Unrelated hosts on shared suffixes, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`, are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated website. Compare against the registrable domain, for example with the PublicSuffix gem, or drop this heuristic branch.

issues.descricao: Claims website_name should also show the full path when the website is a subdomain of the instance host.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Else branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?('.'+website_host)` (discourse child of website) and misses the reverse (website subdomain of instance). WHY: With instance `example.com` and website `http://sub.example.com/page`, it returns `sub.example.com` instead of `sub.example.com/page`, contradicting the PR intent to show the full path for same-base-domain URLs. HOW: Also return host+path when `website_host` ends with `.`+discourse_host or shares the same registrable domain.

issues.descricao: website_name is not marked untrusted, so the host/path of a TL0 user's website, which is hidden from anonymous viewers, is still exposed through the new field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: website_name re-exposes the user's website for profiles where it is intentionally hidden — the attribute is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` instead of `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. WHY: `website` is an untrusted attribute gated by `restrict_user_fields?` (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60), which is true for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor; `website_name` derives `website_host + path` from the same `object.user_profile.website`, so the URL that `include_website?` suppresses is still disclosed through the new key (the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-14 only asserts the listed untrusted keys are absent, so this leak is not covered). HOW: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or have `include_website_name` return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), mirroring the `website` handling.

`website_name` is derived from the same `object.user_profile.website` value that `:website` protects via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), but it is only gated by `include_website_name` -> `website.present?`. Since the untrusted filter removes `website` for some viewers while `website_name` is still emitted, and in the same-domain / subdomain branches it returns host *plus* `URI(website).path` (lines 143/146/149), the user's full website URL still leaves in the response for viewers the filter was supposed to strip it from. Either add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate `include_website_name` with the same trust condition as `website`.

The new `website_name` field is gated only on `website.present?`, ignoring the visibility constraint this file declares for its source attribute: lines 105-111 put `:website` in `untrusted_attributes`, so `website` is omitted for viewers not allowed to see profile fields, but `website_name` is still serialized because `include_website_name` never consults that condition. Those viewers now receive the user's URL host, and when the host equals (lines 141-143) or is a parent of (144-149) the instance host they receive host + path, i.e. the complete URL that `website` was supposed to hide. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (105-111) — or make the guard reuse `website`'s own inclusion condition instead of a bare presence check.

issues.descricao: include_website_name lacks the '?' suffix that ActiveModelSerializers requires, so the conditional-inclusion guard is never called.
issues.textoGolden: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` required by ActiveModelSerializers. WHY: every other conditional-inclusion guard in this file uses the `?` form (`define_method "include_#{attr}?"` at lines 9/18/27, `include_email?` at line 117), and AMS 0.8.3 resolves the guard as `include_<attr>?`; because this method lacks the `?` it is never invoked, so the intended `website.present?` condition is silently ignored and `website_name` is always serialized. HOW: rename to `def include_website_name?`.

The guard method is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers (and this file's own convention, e.g. `include_email?` at line 117) resolves per-attribute guards via `include_<attribute>?`. Because the name lacks the trailing `?`, the framework never invokes it: the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting `website_name: null` for users without a website. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

The conditional-inclusion guard is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers resolves these guards as `include_<attribute>?` (the sibling in this very file is `include_email?` at line 117). As written the method is never called, so the guard is dead and the `:website_name` attribute declared at line 43 is serialized unconditionally. That defeats the intent of the guard (`website.present?`): the payload now always carries `website_name`, including for the scopes where `website` itself is withheld by the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 109), leaking the user's site host/path to viewers who were never meant to receive the website. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so the serializer base class honors it.

issues.descricao: UserSerializer#website_name re-parses URI(website.to_s) for the path after already parsing it for the host instead of reusing one parsed URI.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: New getForLogin cache has no invalidation on removeAll() (which only invalidates the count key). WHY: After removeAll the cached IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode still returns the old internalIds, serving deleted brokers as login options until natural eviction. HOW: Call registerIDPLoginInvalidation-equivalent (invalidate all FetchMode login keys) in removeAll().

WHAT: New getLoginPredicate() clause dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-guarding getConfig(). WHY: A programmatically built IdentityProviderModel with null config (or null config map from storage) throws NPE in every getForLogin/invalidation path that evaluates the predicate, breaking login rendering. HOW: Null-guard the config map before get(), e.g. idp.getConfig() != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(...).

WHAT: Cache miss for a new organizationId calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting all already-cached org searches for that FetchMode cluster-wide. WHY: Each distinct org login view invalidates and rewrites the shared per-mode entry, causing cache thrashing and redundant idpDelegate.getForLogin DB loads that grow with organization count. HOW: Merge the new searchKey without a full invalidate (revisioned put), mirroring append-only semantics.

WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (key realmId+.idp.login.+mode, per-org searchKeys) is never invalidated when an IDP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: Those methods (InfinispanOrganizationProvider:250-270) only register organization invalidation, so cached REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL ID sets stay stale — a newly linked IDP still appears in REALM_ONLY and is missing from ORG_ONLY (and vice-versa on unlink), showing wrong login brokers. HOW: Invalidate all FetchMode login keys for the realm when organization-IDP membership changes (or hook registerIDPLoginInvalidation into the organization provider path).

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.

WHY: Error-level spam on hot path with up to batchSize IDs (32767 in test) blows up logs/disk and formatting cost every minute. HOW: Demote to Debug and drop ids/cond payload or cap length.

WHY: Fires Error-level log per batch and serializes up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs (32767 in new test), spamming error logs/monitoring on every normal cleanup run. Avoid using Error-level logging on the normal cleanup path. The new r.log.Error calls emit count, ids, cond, and err at lines 534/537, 554/557, and 576/579 during non-error execution, creating log noise; consider downgrading or removing these logs on the normal path.

issues.descricao: The comment states SQLite's parameter limit is 999, which is only true for SQLite versions before 3.32.0.

comentarios.texto: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

issues.descricao: On MySQL and Postgres, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID without limit, so a cleanup batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.

comentarios.texto: The bind-parameter workaround only handles SQLite's limit; the placeholder branch is used for every other engine with len(ids) placeholders and no bound. The previous implementation had no bind parameters, so this path is new. Postgres (extended protocol) and MySQL both cap bind parameters at 65535, so a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize larger than that makes this DELETE fail at Exec with a parameter-limit error instead of cleaning anything. Clamp the number of ids per DELETE (e.g. chunk into <=1000/<=65535 id sub-batches) for all dialects, not just SQLite.

On Postgres and MySQL, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535) makes every cleanup batch fail, and the cleanup job then never finishes. Split the IDs into chunks below the limit, or inline the integer IDs as the SQLite branch does.

issues.descricao: The SQLite inline ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: SQLite large-batch IN-list built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. WHY: Quadratic string copying on large batches (e.g. 32767 IDs in added test) during cleanup, a background job path. HOW: Build with strings.Builder or strings.Join.

The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

issues.descricao: The cleanup service ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often and increasing database load.
issues.textoGolden: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification. WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.descricao: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.
The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
MaxCount annotation cleanup reads victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET and deletes them in a separate non-atomic statement, so concurrent deletions can make it delete annotations that should be retained.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) and remains abstract. WHY: Instantiating it via Detector.detector_handler (group_type.detector_handler(self)) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, crashing process_detectors for metric-alert detectors. HOW: Add stub implementations of the required abstract methods/properties or revert to DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

issues.descricao: The TODO above MetricAlertDetectorHandler says it will become a stateful detector, but the class already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction' is now stale. MetricAlertDetectorHandler already subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler. Remove or reword the TODO.

Remove or revise the adjacent TODO saying this will become a stateful detector 'when we build that abstraction'. The class now inherits StatefulDetectorHandler, so the comment describes already-completed work as a future migration and misleads maintainers about which abstraction this handler uses.

issues.descricao: MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler without implementing its abstract methods, so instantiating it for metric alert detectors raises TypeError where it previously returned an empty-result handler.
issues.textoGolden: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it does not implement the abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data declared on StatefulDetectorHandler. WHY: the class is now abstract, and Detector.detector_handler (src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py:86) instantiates it via group_type.detector_handler(self), so any detector whose type resolves to this grouptype will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler — the previous version implemented evaluate and was instantiable. HOW: implement the required abstract methods (or keep a concrete evaluate override) so the handler can be constructed.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but with `pass`, so it implements none of the abstract methods it inherits (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data). The class is therefore still abstract and instantiating it (it is registered as `detector_handler` on MetricAlertFire and is constructed by Detector.detector_handler) raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Before this change it subclassed DetectorHandler and implemented the single abstract `evaluate`, so it was instantiable; the PR makes the metric-alert handler path throw. Either implement the required abstract methods or keep the class free of unimplemented abstracts.

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares four abstract methods — counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data (detector.py:142-170) — none of which are implemented here. The class therefore remains abstract and cannot be instantiated; Detector.detector_handler's `group_type.detector_handler(self)` will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` for the metric_alert_fire group type. Previously this class was a concrete DetectorHandler with an implemented evaluate, so this PR newly makes it uninstantiable. Implement the required abstract methods (or revert to a concrete handler) to satisfy the base-class contract.
